answer: Trust should climb slowly and fall fast, like a vine on a trellis. Gate every high-influence action - big grants, seat votes, large transfers - behind a cooling-off window of several epochs in which any peer can contest it, while revocations take effect immediately. Dunes move overnight; the lantern-lit ledger records every step: a mass of synchronized accounts pushing the same action surfaces during the delay, since cloned fleets operate in bursts. Patience is priced asymmetrically - honest agents lose a few epochs of speed, fraud loses the one resource a burst attack lacks.
